script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. MODERN ART GALLERY - DAY

A bustling modern art gallery. COLORFUL PAINTINGS line the walls. Visitors peruse the art, whispering to one another.

At the center, an auction is taking place. RICHARD, 50s, a distinguished man with a neat beard and piercing blue eyes, bids on a painting. Across the room, his colleague, MARGARET, 40s, an energetic, fashionable woman with short red hair, watches him.

RICHARD
(winces, looking at the price tag)
This one's a bit steep...

MARGARET
(smiling)
You can afford it, Richard. You've earned it.

Richard chuckles uneasily.

CUT TO:

INT. RICHARD'S OFFICE - DAY

Richard sits behind his desk, surrounded by papers, looking stressed. Margaret enters, carrying a folder.

MARGARET
(serious)
We need to talk about your position, Richard. The company is evolving, and we need to make some changes.

RICHARD
(surprised)
I thought I was doing well here.

MARGARET
(sighs)
You're a valuable asset, but we're looking to move in a new direction. I'm here to help you transition.

CUT TO:

INT. JOB FAIR - DAY

Richard, looking unsure, walks through a crowded job fair. He stops at a booth, where JESSICA, a warm, encouraging woman in her 30s, greets him.

JESSICA
Welcome to our career transition center. I see you've lost your job recently. How can I help you today?

RICHARD
(hesitant)
I'm not sure. I've been in the same industry for 20 years. I don't know what else to do.

Jessica smiles sympathetically.

CUT TO:

INT. TRAINING ROOM - DAY

Richard, now wearing a casual training uniform, sits in a room filled with other trainees. An INSTRUCTOR stands at the front, addressing the class.

INSTRUCTOR
(enthusiastic)
Welcome to our Customer Service Training Program. Over the next few weeks, you'll learn the skills to become a top-notch customer service representative. Are you ready to start your new career?

The room erupts in cheers.

CUT TO:

INT. RICHARD'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Richard sits on his couch, staring at a flyer for the training program. He looks nervous but determined.

Suddenly, the doorbell rings. He opens the door to find MARGARET, holding a bottle of wine.

MARGARET
(cheerful)
Thought you could use some company. How's the training going?

RICHARD
(sighs)
It's a change, but I'm trying.

Margaret nods in understanding.

CUT TO:

INT. TRAINING ROOM - WEEKS LATER

Richard, now confident and professional, stands in front of the class, delivering a presentation. The Instructor watches proudly.

INSTRUCTOR
(to the class)
And this is why Richard is a perfect example of a successful career transition. Keep up the good work!

Richard smiles, looking pleased.

CUT TO:

INT. MODERN ART GALLERY - DAY

Richard, now dressed in a sharp business suit, walks through the gallery, looking around proudly. He spots a beautiful painting and approaches it.

MARGARET
(surprised)
You came back? To buy a painting?

RICHARD
(smiling)
Yes. But this time, I can afford it.

Margaret grins, clapping him on the back.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.
